target_customer: Developers and teams that are heavy users of Claude Code
problem: About 88 percent of a Claude Code token bill is tool input and output, so users overpay for non reasoning tokens.
business_model: Developer tool subscription at $20 per month or 10 percent of savings generated
product_category: AI developer tools, token cost optimization

founders.name: Saahil Sundaresan
education: Stanford, BS and MS in CS and linguistics

competitors.name: Compresr (YC W26)
competitors.what: Context Gateway proxy that compresses tool outputs for coding agents

competitors.name: The Token Company (YC W26)
competitors.what: Compression model that preprocesses LLM inputs

competitors.name: Edgee
competitors.what: Drop in compression proxy for Claude Code and other coding tools

technical_complexity.rationale: A wrapper and proxy that compresses context while preserving quality needs careful evaluation (the company uses its own SessionBench), but is buildable by two engineers.

defensibility.rationale: Sits on top of a third party product and several YC peers and open source tools do the same job.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not yet known; Anthropic can add context compression and caching natively.

market_need_then: Claude Code costs are large for heavy users; the company reports 34 to 51 percent savings (average 47 percent) in its own benchmarks, while a third party benchmark found 19 percent for one tool of this type.

branding.name_origin: The product Fermat's Last Token plays on Fermat's Last Theorem and the margin note, per the company site; the company name Quotient Labs is not explained.

identity.voice_and_tone: Humorous: unserious people doing serious work

branding.brand_signature: Fermat's Last Token product name and margin too narrow joke

brand_strength.rationale: The product name is witty and memorable for developers, but no outside press about the brand was found.

outcome_analysis: Quotient Labs is an active Winter 2026 company selling a Claude Code cost saver with a witty product brand. No verified funding exists beyond an unconfirmed $125K seed on one aggregator. The outcome is open, and the main risks are Anthropic shipping native savings and several YC peers building the same tool.
notes: Unverified: Dealroom (single aggregator, AI generated text) lists a $125K seed with no investor or date; not recorded as a round. Competitor source dates are approximate (2026). No outcome news found. The Fermat's Last Theorem search returned unrelated Anthropic news and no coverage of the company.
